decisions.rationale: Verified at f18bccaf. The 'Who points at whom' figcaption in authoring/evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/crud-aggregates-and-joins/page-build/src/seeding-sample-data.body.html (added in loop 1 for C2E-SEED-04) reads "lead_id points at another instructor, the person's team lead, so within one INSERT a lead's row comes before the rows that point at it." Replayed in the page's own simulator on EMPTY_TABLES: INSERT INTO instructors (instructor_id, name, lead_id) VALUES (2, 'Tomas', 1), (1, 'Mara', NULL); prints INSERT 0 2. The sentence also contradicts the teaching two lines above ("These foreign keys are checked as each INSERT finishes"). The cited SET CONSTRAINTS documentation (NOT DEFERRABLE is always IMMEDIATE, checked at the end of each statement) agrees with the simulator; no server was run. So the clause teaches a false checking model right before Activity 2 asks learners to reason about it. Remedy (a), REVERT: delete the loop-1 clause ", so within one INSERT a lead's row comes before the rows that point at it", restoring the 8a7daa17 wording for that piece (8a7daa17 had no such clause). This reopens nothing material: the first half of the same loop-1 sentence ("lead_id points at another instructor, the person's team lead") is true and still answers C2E-SEED-04's main point, and SEED-04's hint-1 remark is harmless because either instructors or students can safely run first. If the task owner counts the whole caption addition as one indivisible edit, revert the caption to 8a7daa17's "Who points at whom (foreign keys)". That reopens C2E-SEED-04 (low: lead_id and the self-reference unexplained), which is far less harmful than leaving a false rule. Remedy (b), leave, is rejected: it ships wrong teaching. Mirror the revert in artifact.md.
